title: Amortized token SKU & regional blend workbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working spreadsheet-style dump for an amortized per-call SKU and regional token blend — focused on answering: how much does a single API call actually cost across models and regions once we amortize infra, licensing, and ops overhead?

High-level approach (tabs):
- summary: blended per-token COGS + margin by model family and region (this doc)
- components: raw line-items (GPU time, infra VM, network egress, storage, license, SRE, monitoring)
- scenarios: sensitivity rows for batching/kv cache/quantization
- allocation: rules for amortizing reserved capacity and license commitments

Key assumptions (editable):
1) Baseline GPU spot-equivalent cost (amortized) = $1.20/hr (effective across our contracts)
2) Average exec time per 1k tokens (baseline model-family A / 16k context) = 0.45s per 1k tokens (seq-latency averaged)
3) Network egress average = $0.007 per 1k tokens (includes LB + egress multipliers per region)
4) SRE/monitoring/infra ops overhead target = 8% of gross COGS (can be changed by region)
5) License/third-party model fee = variable per model family (A: $0.00, B: $0.02 per 1k tokens, C: $0.09 per 1k tokens)
6) Amortization window for reserved capacity = 12 months; reserve discount applied where dedicated/committed pools exist
7) Token definition = input + output tokens aggregated; typical call = 350 tokens request + 650 tokens response = 1000 tokens

Summary table (columns explained, values are per-1k-token basis):
Columns: model_family | region | gpu_time_s_per_1k | gpu_cost_per_1k | infra_misc_per_1k | network_per_1k | license_per_1k | op_overhead_per_1k | total_cogs_per_1k | list_price_per_1k | gross_margin_pct

Example rows (baseline):
ModelA | us-west1 | 0.45 | =0.45*(1.20/3600) -> $0.00015 | $0.00040 | $0.00700 | $0.00000 | =8%*(sum prior columns) -> $0.00057 | $0.00812 | $0.01200 | 32.3%
ModelB | eu-west1 | 0.55 | =0.55*(1.25/3600) -> $0.00019 | $0.00045 | $0.00850 | $0.02000 | $0.00190 | $0.03104 | $0.01800 | -72.9% (loss)
ModelC | ap-southeast1 | 0.70 | =0.70*(1.40/3600) -> $0.00027 | $0.00060 | $0.01000 | $0.09000 | $0.00899 | $0.10986 | $0.03000 | -266.2%

Notes on above: list_price_per_1k is current hosted API SKU in that region for family. Negative margins indicate areas where we rely on reserved capacity or need price adjustments / routing.

Formulas (text form you can drop into a sheet):
- gpu_cost_per_1k = gpu_time_s_per_1k * (gpu_hourly_effective_cost / 3600)
- op_overhead_per_1k = overhead_pct * (gpu_cost_per_1k + infra_misc_per_1k + network_per_1k + license_per_1k)
- total_cogs_per_1k = sum(gpu_cost_per_1k, infra_misc_per_1k, network_per_1k, license_per_1k, op_overhead_per_1k)
- gross_margin_pct = (list_price_per_1k - total_cogs_per_1k) / list_price_per_1k

Scenario snapshots (quick sensitivity):
1) Batching x2 (reduce gpu_time_s_per_1k by 25% due to increased batching efficiency for typical request mix):
- impact: gpu_cost_per_1k down ~25%, total_cogs down ~15–18% depending on license. Example ModelB eu-west1 margin improves from -72.9% to -28.4% (still negative but much closer).
2) 4-bit quantization path (model family compatible -> license reduced but inference slower by +5% latency -> gpu_time_s_per_1k *1.05 but license_per_1k halved):
- net: positive for expensive-license models (ModelC moves from -266% to -140% on list price unchanged).
3) Reserve-commit shift (70% traffic pinned to reserved pools -> effective gpu_hourly drops to $0.60/hr for that share):
- net: blended cogs improves materially; region-heavy customers see margins improve enough to support current list price.

Allocation rules (short):
- Reserved GPU amortization: allocate reserved monthly cost to model families weighted by 30-day token volume and peak concurrency buckets.
- License pass-through: per-call where applicable. If model runs in-house and license fixed monthly, amortize by last-30d token share.
- Edge/network CDN: allocate egress by region tag of request path, but charge back adjusted egress for replicate caching (i.e., cached responses subtract network_per_1k by estimated cache-hit-rate).

Open questions / to validate:
- Confirm GPU-hourly effective numbers per region (infra has a new pricing sheet; ask infra-finance for raw).
- Confirm whether license per-1k for ModelC can be negotiated under volume tiers (GH-rr/runtime-824 references negotiation thread).
- Validate average tokens per call by customer segment (PLG vs enterprise are different; we should have two columns).
- Decide default overhead_pct regionally (currently flat 8% but APAC infra ops are higher historically).

Quick sensitivity table (example values):
Scenario | ModelB eu-west1 total_cogs_per_1k | list_price | margin
Baseline | $0.03104 | $0.01800 | -72.9%
Batching x2 | $0.02082 | $0.01800 | -15.7%
Batching x2 + Reserve commit | $0.01250 | $0.01800 | 30.6%
Quant4 + batching | $0.01890 | $0.01800 | -5.0%

Recommendations & action items (ranked):
1) Priority: implement a short-term routing rule that prefers reserved-backed pools for high-license models in eu-west1 and ap-southeast1. Owner: Marcus Chen. ETA: 3 weeks. Impact: immediate margin recovery for ModelB/C.
2) Medium: surface a per-customer token-profile in billing UI so we can enforce batching-friendly SDK defaults for PLG customers. Owner: Lina Rodriguez. ETA: 8 weeks. Impact: reduces baseline gpu_time_s_per_1k by ~10–20%.
3) Low: aggressive license renegotiation for ModelC (volume tiers) and evaluate switching to community license variants where quality acceptable. Owner: Ethan Brooks + BizDev. ETA: Q2.
4) Data: ask analytics to produce 30-day distribution of tokens-per-call broken out by customer segment + region. Ticket: JIRA-OPT-57. Owner: Data team. ETA: 1 week.

Quick notes for next pass (what to add into the sheet):
- Add a tab to model-family-level quantization readiness (accuracy delta vs savings) with sample prompts and model evals.
- Add reserve-commit amortization calculator (slice by pool, months remaining, utilization).
- Add CLI/SDK toggles and assumptions for batch window defaults; measure effect on P95 latency vs cost.

Slack references: convo with infra-finance on 2025-02-20 (thread: #infra-costs-reserve) has raw GPU numbers. BizDev negotiation notes in GH-rr/runtime-824.

Bottom line (working):
We are currently losing money on high-license model families in certain regions at current posted SKUs. There are three levers that give high ROI and are relatively quick: routing to reserved pools, small-batching defaults for PLG traffic, and license renegotiation. This workbook is intentionally conservative on op overhead; adjust once infra-finance passes region-specific hourly costs.

Draft status: ideas fleshed out but requires data feeds (GPU effective hourly by region, per-customer token distribution, license volume tiers).

TODOs (short):

- [ ] Data: produce tokens-per-call segments (1w) - JIRA-OPT-57
- [ ] Lina: prototype SDK batch-by-default toggle in playground (6w)

End of sheet dump (save as: amortized-token-sku-blend-sheet, then convert components into a proper Google Sheet when data is available).
